reasoning_content:
The write succeeded (rc=0), but the type still shows "threaded" (root: "domain threaded", docker: "threaded"). So the file accepted the write but the mode didn't change — this suggests the write had no effect (maybe the file is read-only? No, rc=0 was returned). Hmm, actually cgroup.type is read-only. Let me double-check: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.type` outputs "domain threaded" — so the root cgroup is both "domain" and "threaded"? This is a weird state. And docker's cgroup type is "threaded".

Maybe the write to cgroup.threads was accepted but had no effect because... actually, for a "threaded" cgroup, writing 0 should switch it to domain mode. Unless the controller is busy.

Let me test whether the write actually changes anything: check the value of cgroup.threads.

action.command: cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.threads; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/docker/cgroup.threads; echo ---; echo 1 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.threads 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.type /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.threads
